'''Jack Thomson Moyer''' (March 7, 1929 – January 10, 2004) was a marine biologist and known child sexual abuser from [[Kansas]], who lived for most of his life on [[Miyake-jima]] in [[Japan]]. Moyer was a scientist with the [[United States Air Force]], who became a teacher later in life for the [[American School in Japan]] (ASIJ). He committed suicide in 2004. After his death, multiple allegations surfaced that Moyer had sexually molested students during his tenure at the ASIJ.

== Life and career ==

Jack Moyer was born on 7 March 1929, in Kansas, United States.

He made his first visit to Japan in 1951 with the United States Air Force, and made his first trip to Miyake-jima the following year. During his time in Japan, Moyer saw that the Air Force was using [[Onoharajima]] as a practice bombing range. Moyer wrote a letter to an associate of President [[Harry S. Truman]] to stop the bombing in order to save a rare seabird, the [[Japanese murrelet]], that breeds on Onoharajima. The bombing was stopped.<ref name=obit>{{cite web|author1=Stephen Hesse|title='Miyake man' leaves a legacy of inspiration|date=15 January 2004 |url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/life/2004/01/15/environment/miyake-man-leaves-a-legacy-of-inspiration/#.U8bZ5I1dUWE|publisher=The Japan Times|accessdate=16 July 2014}}</ref> Moyer later moved to Miyake-jima in 1957 after graduating from [[Colgate University]], and became a part of the island community for over 50&nbsp;years.

Moyer received a master's from the [[University of Michigan]] and attained his doctorate in marine ecology from the [[University of Tokyo]].<ref>[http://web-japan.org/trends/people/peo030702.html Jack T. Moyer | People | Trends in Japan | Web Japan<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Moyer was an [[Ornithology|ornithologist]], marine biologist and naturalist who focused on the islands of the [[Izu Islands|Izu archipelago]] and promoted the need for preservation of the islands' unique ecology. Having spent many years on Miyake-jima, he was aware of the changes that came with modernization. Construction of public roads and harbors claimed increasing amounts of previously untouched mountain forest areas of the islands, and increasing car traffic and sea pollution were important concerns of his as well. During his time on Miyake-jima, Moyer organized a summer school for local children.<ref>{{cite web|author1=Satoko Seino|title=Toward the Revival of Miyake-jima After the Latest Volcanic Eruption|url=http://www.coremoc.go.jp/en/report/coralreefjapan/column_miyakejima.pdf|accessdate=16 July 2014|archive-date=19 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130119071400/http://www.coremoc.go.jp/en/report/coralreefjapan/column_miyakejima.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1996, he was awarded the [[Asahi Shimbun]] prize for his work on ocean ecology and the education of young children.<ref name=ASIJ>{{cite news|author1=Jon Mitchell|title=ASIJ admits honored teacher sexually abused students|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2014/03/20/national/asij-admits-honored-teacher-sexually-abused-students/#.U8bcjo1dUWH|newspaper=The Japan Times|accessdate=16 July 2014}}</ref>

Later in life, Moyer split his time between Miyake-jima and Tokyo, where he taught a course entitled "Japan Lands And People" (JLAP) at the American School in Japan (ASIJ). Moyer was an extremely popular teacher at the school.<ref name=obit /> A highlight of the JLAP course was the annual week-long trip to Miyake-jima for the 7th grade ASIJ class, where they would stay in Moyer's modest island home while studying local fisheries and farming.

Moyer wrote several articles for the ''[[Japan Times]]'' on the marine biology of Japan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jack T. Moyer|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/author/int-jack_t-_moyer/|publisher=The Japan Times|accessdate=16 July 2014}}</ref> He was the author of several books, including ''Dolphin interpreter Introduction'' {{ISBN|4861640032}} and ''Man of the sea and the birds'' {{ISBN|4886221092}}.

Along with the other residents of the island, Moyer was forced to flee the island following the eruptions of [[Mount Ōyama (Kanagawa)|Mount Oyama]] in 2000. Later, he was asked by the [[Tokyo Metropolitan Government|Tokyo Metropolitan government]] to survey the island. He concluded that the island's ecology was recovering.

== Death ==

Moyer committed suicide at age 74 in his Tokyo home in 2004.<ref name=Suicide>{{cite web|url=http://www.cdnn.info/eco/e040111c/e040111c.html |access-date=2008-02-21 |title=Famed conservationist Jack Moyer commits suicide in Tokyo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927234538/http://www.cdnn.info/eco/e040111c/e040111c.html |archive-date=September 27, 2007 }}</ref> Moyer left behind two suicide notes, and his body was discovered among a batch of unidentified sleeping pills.<ref name=Suicide />

== Scandal ==
In March 2014, The American School in Japan admitted that several alumni had been sexually abused as middle school students by Moyer, while he was a teacher at the school. As many as 32 girls were victimized by Moyer, starting as early as 1964.<ref>Mitchell, John. "[http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2014/03/20/national/asij-admits-honored-teacher-sexually-abused-students/#.Uysq7a1dVzC ASIJ admits honored teacher sexually abused students]" ([https://web.archive.org/web/20140525221839/http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2014/03/20/national/asij-admits-honored-teacher-sexually-abused-students/ Archive]). ''[[The Japan Times]]''. March 20, 2014. Retrieved on May 28, 2014.</ref> In 2014, a legal firm representing 10 women who had allegedly been victims of Moyer's sent a demand letter to the ASIJ, claiming the school had been told repeatedly about Moyer's actions, but did nothing.<ref name=Oregon>{{cite web|author1=Amiee Green|title=American School in Japan told pedophile teacher abused girls for decades, Portland firm says|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/portland/index.ssf/2014/06/portland_lawyers_send_letter_t.html|website=Oregonlive|date=13 June 2014 |accessdate=16 July 2014}}</ref>

In June 2015, the ASIJ Board of Directors released a letter admitting that an independent investigation found that Jack Moyer's abuse of students was extensive and that the abuse was covered up by faculty and administrators for years.  The board apologized for the harm this has caused and promised to release the report in English and Japanese by mid-June, 2015.<ref name=BoardAdmission>{{cite web|author1=Tomohiro Osaki|title=American School in Japan admits covering up teacher's sex abuse for decades|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2015/06/05/national/crime-legal/american-school-japan-admits-covering-teachers-sex-abuse-decades/#.VXG-4_9VhBc|website=The Japan Times|date=5 June 2015 |accessdate=5 June 2015}}</ref>  The full report, released by [[Ropes & Gray]] LLP on June 15, 2015, concluded "[i]n light of all of the evidence we have examined, it is apparent to us that Moyer was a serial pedophile who, in our assessment, sexually abused female ASIJ students".<ref name=BoardReport>{{cite web|url=http://community.asij.ac.jp/file/Ropes-report-and-survivor-statements.pdf|title=The Ropes & Gray report of sexual abuse by Jack Moyer|publisher=American School in Japan|page=30|access-date=15 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701125737/http://community.asij.ac.jp/file/Ropes-report-and-survivor-statements.pdf|archive-date=1 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=BoardReportNews>{{cite web|author1=Tomohiro Osaki|title=ASIJ sex abouse report is finally released, blames 'culteral taboos'|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2015/06/15/national/asij-sex-abuse-report-finally-released-blames-cultural-taboos/|website=The Japan Times|date=15 June 2015 |accessdate=15 June 2015}}</ref>  Lawyers for 13 of the victims also released their report on June 15, 2015.<ref name=VictimsReport>{{cite web |url=http://crewjanci.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/CREW-JANCI-FINAL-REPORT-ON-ASIJ.pdf|title=Report on the Sexual Abuse of Students at the American School in Japan|publisher=Crew Janci LLP|access-date=15 June 2015}}</ref>

== Taxon named after Moyer ==
*'''''[[Synchiropus moyeri]]''''', the '''Moyer's dragonet''', is a [[species]] of fish in the family [[dragonet|Callionymidae]], the dragonets. It is found in the Western Pacific.<ref>Zaiser, M.J. and R. Fricke, 1985. Synchiropus moyeri, a new species of dragonet (Callionymidae) from Miyake-jima, Japan. Jap. J. Ichthyol. 31(4):389-397.</ref>
